entry.label: The Second Law of Technodynamics — Velitchkov (2026)
entry.description: Velitchkov proposes that control over coordination terms tends to concentrate without counter-action. Counter-action may itself create another concentration. The proposed tendency is contestable; the article does not establish concentration alone as a cause of collapse.
entry.canonical_definition: An attributed proposal by Ivo Velitchkov concerning the concentration of control over coordination terms.

profile.title: The Second Law of Technodynamics
profile.summary: Velitchkov proposes that coordination control tends to concentrate without counter-action. Control concerns the ability to set or change terms on which others depend and which they cannot readily replace. Counter-action can itself create another concentration.
profile.canonical_definition: An attributed proposal by Ivo Velitchkov concerning the concentration of control over coordination terms.
profile.why_it_matters: The proposal asks who can change participation terms, and what an effective alternative would require.
profile.context_and_lineage: The SysCoI discovery record is retained. The conference account and two public articles provide a more detailed, attributed account.
profile.editorial_note: The older linked Productive Organisational Paradoxes deck is a different presentation. De Visch uses autonomy in a distinct human-developmental sense.
key_distinctions: Participatory discretion and the opportunities enabled by participation are distinct.
The thermodynamics comparison is a mnemonic, not a physical equivalence.
The full article does not establish concentration alone as a cause of collapse.
common_misreadings: A proposed tendency is not a demonstrated universal law.
open_checks: Audio and on-screen visuals have not been independently checked against the auto-generated captions.
